notebooks.title: End to end
notebooks.blurb: One notebook for any supported model: train a baseline if needed, prune, fine-tune, quantize, evaluate, report.

cells.source:
# CompressKit — end-to-end on Kaggle (one notebook, **Run All**)

`train FP32 baseline → gradual prune + fine-tune → quantize (always last) → evaluate the exported .onnx → report`

**Before running:** right panel → *Accelerator: GPU T4*, *Internet: ON*. For the HAR model, *Add Input* →
*Human Action Recognition (HAR) Dataset*. Then edit only the config cell below.

Outputs land in `/kaggle/working/compresskit_output/`: the final `model.onnx`, `report.html`, `results.json`.
**Latency in this run is Kaggle-CPU latency**, not your deployment target — measure that with
`compresskit bench model.onnx` on the target machine (see the last cell).

# ======================= CONFIG — the only cell you edit =======================
MODEL      = "har_resnet18"   # "har_resnet18" | "resnet20" | "resnet56" | "vgg16_bn" | "custom"
MODE       = "manual"         # "manual": you choose the schedule | "auto": give a budget, it finds the least compression

# --- manual mode ---
PRUNE_RATIO = 0.5             # fraction of channels to remove
STEPS       = 5               # gradual pruning steps
FT_EPOCHS   = 5               # fine-tune epochs after each step
LOSS        = "dkd"           # "kd" | "dkd"

# --- auto mode (accuracy/size budgets are valid on Kaggle; a latency budget would be Kaggle-CPU latency) ---
BUDGET      = "accuracy_drop<1%,size<5mb"

PRECISION   = "int8"          # Kaggle's CPU has no fast INT8, but we still build the INT8 model for your target
TRAIN_EPOCHS = None           # None = default (60 for CIFAR models, 10 for pretrained HAR/custom)

# --- bring your own data / model (MODEL = "custom") ---
DATA_DIR    = "/kaggle/input/my-dataset"   # one sub-folder per class
INPUT_SIZE  = 224
MODEL_FILE  = None            # path to a .pt saved with compresskit's save_model; None = train a pretrained ResNet-18
# ===============================================================================

import os, subprocess, sys, shutil, json, pathlib
REPO = "https://github.com/Bhagyesh0603/Model-Compression-ToolKit..git"
if not os.path.exists("/kaggle/working/compresskit_repo"):
    subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", REPO, "/kaggle/working/compresskit_repo"], check=True)
os.chdir("/kaggle/working/compresskit_repo")
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "-e", "."], check=True)

import torch
print("GPU:", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else "NONE — enable GPU in the right panel, then Restart & Run All")

ARCH, DATASET, DATA_ROOT = {
    "har_resnet18": ("har_resnet18", "har", None),
    "resnet20":     ("resnet20", "cifar10", None),
    "resnet56":     ("resnet56", "cifar10", None),
    "vgg16_bn":     ("vgg16_bn", "cifar10", None),
    "custom":       ("har_resnet18", "folder", DATA_DIR),
}[MODEL]

OUT  = pathlib.Path("/kaggle/working/compresskit_output"); OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
WORK = "/kaggle/working/work"
CKPT = MODEL_FILE or f"checkpoints/{MODEL}_fp32.pt"

def run(args):
    args = [str(a) for a in args]
    print("$ compresskit", " ".join(args), flush=True)
    code = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "compresskit.cli", *args]).returncode
    return code

data_args = ["--dataset", DATASET, "--input-size", INPUT_SIZE] + (["--data-root", DATA_ROOT] if DATA_ROOT else [])
## 1 · Train the FP32 baseline (skipped if the checkpoint already exists)
## 2 · Compress: gradual prune + fine-tune → quantize → evaluate the .onnx

common = ["--model", CKPT, *data_args, "--precision", PRECISION, "--allow-slow-int8", "--workdir", WORK,
          "--report", OUT / "report.html", "--json", OUT / "results.json", "--loss", LOSS]
if MODE == "manual":
    code = run(["pipeline", *common, "--prune", PRUNE_RATIO, "--steps", STEPS, "--fine-tune-epochs", FT_EPOCHS])
else:
    code = run(["compress", *common, "--budget", BUDGET, "--steps", STEPS, "--fine-tune-epochs", FT_EPOCHS])
print("exit code", code, "(auto mode returns 1 if the budget was not met — the best attempt is still saved)")
## 3 · Collect the outputs

results = json.loads((OUT / "results.json").read_text())
final = results["stages"][-1]
shutil.copy(final["artifact"], OUT / "model.onnx")
base = results["baseline"]
print(f"accuracy : {base['accuracy']*100:.2f}% -> {final['accuracy']*100:.2f}%  (drop {results['totals']['accuracy_drop_pp']:.2f} pp)")
print(f"size     : {base['size_mb']:.2f} MB -> {final['size_mb']:.2f} MB  ({results['totals']['size_reduction']:.2f}x smaller)")
print(f"precision: {final['precision']}")
print("(latency in this run was measured on Kaggle's CPU — not your target)")
for f in sorted(OUT.iterdir()): print(f"{f.stat().st_size/1e6:8.2f} MB  {f.name}")
from IPython.display import IFrame, display
display(IFrame(str(OUT / "report.html"), width="100%", height=900))

## 4 · Verify speed on your real target (once, on your own machine)

Download `compresskit_output/` from the *Output* tab, then on the target machine:

```bash
pip install -e .   # the repo
compresskit bench model.onnx --input-shape 1 3 224 224      # 1 3 32 32 for the CIFAR models
```

notebooks.title: ResNet-56
notebooks.blurb: ResNet-56 on CIFAR-10 with a bundled baseline checkpoint, plus a check of the ONNX file against the original.

cells.source:
# Compress ResNet-56 (CIFAR-10) — complete Kaggle notebook

`ResNet-56 (FP32, 56 layers)  →  gradual prune + fine-tune  →  INT8 quantize  →  ONNX  →  verify against the original`

The ResNet-56 baseline (92%+ on CIFAR-10) ships inside the repo, so **no training step**.

**Before Run All** (right panel): *Accelerator → GPU T4*, *Internet → On*.
Optional but saves ~30 min: *Add Input → search "CIFAR-10"* and attach any CIFAR-10 dataset in the
original python-pickle format (it must contain a `cifar-10-batches-py` folder). Otherwise it downloads (170 MB).

Everything lands in `/kaggle/working/` — download `resnet56_compressed.zip` from the *Output* tab.

# ======================= CONFIG =======================
PRUNE_RATIO = 0.5    # fraction of channels removed (0.5 channels ~ 75% fewer parameters)
STEPS       = 5      # gradual pruning steps
FT_EPOCHS   = 5      # fine-tune epochs after every step (25 total)
LOSS        = "dkd"  # "kd" | "dkd"
# ======================================================

import os, subprocess, sys, json, shutil, pathlib
REPO = "https://github.com/Bhagyesh0603/Model-Compression-ToolKit..git"
if not os.path.exists("/kaggle/working/ck"):
    subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", REPO, "/kaggle/working/ck"], check=True)
os.chdir("/kaggle/working/ck")
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "-e", "."], check=True)

import torch
print("GPU:", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else "NONE -> enable GPU in the right panel, then Restart & Run All")
from compresskit.zoo.data import resolve_root
print("CIFAR-10 location:", resolve_root(), "(attached dataset if under /kaggle/input, else it will download)")
assert os.path.exists("checkpoints/resnet56_fp32.pt"), "baseline checkpoint missing from the repo"

def run(*args):
    args = [str(a) for a in args]
    print("$", " ".join(args), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(args).returncode
## 1 · Compress: gradual prune + fine-tune → INT8 → evaluate the .onnx

OUT = "/kaggle/working"
code_ = run(sys.executable, "-m", "compresskit.cli", "pipeline",
            "--model", "checkpoints/resnet56_fp32.pt",
            "--prune", PRUNE_RATIO, "--steps", STEPS, "--fine-tune-epochs", FT_EPOCHS, "--loss", LOSS,
            "--precision", "int8", "--allow-slow-int8",
            "--workdir", f"{OUT}/work", "--report", f"{OUT}/report.html", "--json", f"{OUT}/results.json")
assert code_ == 0, "pipeline failed - read the log above"
## 2 · Does the compressed model actually work? (original vs ONNX on 2000 real test images)

r = json.load(open(f"{OUT}/results.json"))
final_onnx = r["stages"][-1]["artifact"]
shutil.copy(final_onnx, f"{OUT}/model.onnx")
shutil.copy("checkpoints/resnet56_fp32.pt", f"{OUT}/resnet56_fp32.pt")
run(sys.executable, "experiments/verify_onnx.py", "--model", "checkpoints/resnet56_fp32.pt",
    "--onnx", f"{OUT}/model.onnx", "--images", 2000)
## 3 · Summary and download bundle

b, f, t = r["baseline"], r["stages"][-1], r["totals"]
print(f"accuracy : {b['accuracy']*100:.2f}% -> {f['accuracy']*100:.2f}%   (drop {t['accuracy_drop_pp']:.2f} pp)")
print(f"size     : {b['size_mb']:.2f} MB -> {f['size_mb']:.2f} MB   ({t['size_reduction']:.1f}x smaller)")
print(f"precision: {f['precision']}")
print("NOTE: latency in this run is Kaggle-CPU latency, not your device. Measure on the target: compresskit bench model.onnx")

import zipfile
with zipfile.ZipFile(f"{OUT}/resnet56_compressed.zip", "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    for name in ("model.onnx", "report.html", "results.json", "resnet56_fp32.pt"):
        z.write(f"{OUT}/{name}", name)
print("bundle:", f"{OUT}/resnet56_compressed.zip", f"({os.path.getsize(f'{OUT}/resnet56_compressed.zip')/1e6:.1f} MB)")
from IPython.display import IFrame, display
display(IFrame(f"{OUT}/report.html", width="100%", height=900))

## 4 · On your Mac (real speed check, once)

```bash
unzip resnet56_compressed.zip
python experiments/verify_onnx.py --model resnet56_fp32.pt --onnx model.onnx
compresskit bench model.onnx
```

notebooks.title: VGG-16-BN on CIFAR-10
notebooks.blurb: Fine-tune an ImageNet-pretrained VGG-16-BN on CIFAR-10, then compress and evaluate it. Recipe availability does not imply a recorded result for this exact configuration.

cells.source:
# Compress VGG-16-BN (528 MB) on CIFAR-10 — Kaggle notebook, no ImageNet needed

`ImageNet-pretrained VGG-16-BN  →  new 10-class head, fine-tuned on CIFAR-10  →  gradual prune + fine-tune  →  INT8  →  ONNX  →  verify`

A 138 M-parameter, 528 MB model, end to end, using only the CIFAR-10 dataset you already attach to the other notebooks.
CIFAR-10 images are upscaled 32→224 so the network keeps its real size; upscaling adds no detail, it only makes the model big.

**Before Run All** (right panel): *Accelerator → GPU T4*, *Internet → On* (downloads the pretrained weights, 528 MB),
and *Add Input → CIFAR-10* in the python-pickle format (it must contain a `cifar-10-batches-py` folder). Without it the notebook
downloads CIFAR-10 itself, which took about 50 minutes on a slow Kaggle link before.

Batch size, mixed precision (fp16) and the GPU placement of every step are automatic; if a GPU run still reports
"out of GPU memory", set `BATCH` to a smaller number. A pruned checkpoint is saved after every step under `work/`.

Time: the 224×224 training passes dominate. Expect hours, not minutes, on a T4; lower `TRAIN_EPOCHS` / `STEPS` to shorten it.
Accuracy is scored on a fixed 2000-image slice of the test set (the full 10,000 on CPU at every stage would take hours),
so differences under about 1 pp are noise.

Everything lands in `/kaggle/working/` — download `vgg16_cifar10_compressed.zip` from the *Output* tab.

# ======================= CONFIG =======================
ARCH         = "tv:vgg16_bn"  # any torchvision ImageNet model: tv:resnet152, tv:vgg19_bn, ...
TRAIN_EPOCHS = 1      # fine-tune the pretrained model on CIFAR-10 (the "original" we compress)
PRUNE_RATIO  = 0.5    # fraction of channels removed (0.5 -> ~75% fewer parameters)
STEPS        = 3      # gradual pruning steps
FT_EPOCHS    = 1      # fine-tune epochs after every step
LOSS         = "dkd"  # "kd" | "dkd"
BATCH        = "auto"   # "auto" probes the GPU for the largest batch that fits and accumulates up to 64
CRITERION    = "taylor"  # channel importance: "taylor" (loss-aware, GPU) | "magnitude" (fast)
PROTECT      = 2        # prune the 2 most quantization-sensitive layers at half the ratio (0 = off)
CALIB        = 256    # calibration images for INT8 (train split)
TEST_IMAGES  = 2000   # test images used to score every stage
# ======================================================

import os, subprocess, sys, json, shutil, pathlib
REPO = "https://github.com/Bhagyesh0603/Model-Compression-ToolKit..git"
if not os.path.exists("/kaggle/working/ck"):
    subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", REPO, "/kaggle/working/ck"], check=True)
os.chdir("/kaggle/working/ck")
# --no-deps: never let pip swap the GPU build of torch that the platform ships; install only what is missing.
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "--no-deps", "-e", "."], check=True)
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "torch-pruning>=1.5,<2.0", "onnx>=1.16", "onnxruntime>=1.19", "matplotlib"], check=True)

import torch

smi = subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi", "-L"], capture_output=True, text=True) if shutil.which("nvidia-smi") else None
print("nvidia-smi:", smi.stdout.strip() if smi is not None and smi.returncode == 0 else "no NVIDIA GPU visible to this session")
print("GPU:", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else "NONE -> training would take days on CPU; enable a GPU, then Restart & Run All")
from compresskit.zoo.data import resolve_root
print("CIFAR-10 location:", resolve_root(), "(attached dataset if under /kaggle/input, else it will download)")

def run(*args):
    args = [str(a) for a in args]
    print("$", " ".join(args), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(args).returncode

DATA = ["--dataset", "cifar10-upscaled", "--input-size", "224", "--test-samples", str(TEST_IMAGES)]
## 1 · The original: pretrained VGG-16-BN with a CIFAR-10 head, fine-tuned

CKPT = "checkpoints/vgg16_bn_cifar10.pt"
assert run(sys.executable, "-m", "compresskit.cli", "train", "--arch", ARCH, *DATA,
           "--epochs", TRAIN_EPOCHS, "--lr", "0.01", "--batch-size", BATCH, "--out", CKPT) == 0, "training failed - read the log above"
## 2 · Compress: gradual prune + fine-tune → INT8 → evaluate the .onnx

OUT = "/kaggle/working"
code_ = run(sys.executable, "-m", "compresskit.cli", "pipeline", "--model", CKPT, *DATA,
            "--calib", CALIB, "--batch-size", BATCH,
            "--criterion", CRITERION, "--protect-sensitive", PROTECT,
            "--prune", PRUNE_RATIO, "--steps", STEPS, "--fine-tune-epochs", FT_EPOCHS, "--loss", LOSS,
            "--precision", "int8", "--allow-slow-int8",
            "--workdir", f"{OUT}/work", "--report", f"{OUT}/report.html", "--json", f"{OUT}/results.json")
assert code_ == 0, "pipeline failed - read the log above"
## 3 · Does the compressed model actually work? (original vs ONNX on real test images)

r = json.load(open(f"{OUT}/results.json"))
shutil.copy(r["stages"][-1]["artifact"], f"{OUT}/model.onnx")
run(sys.executable, "experiments/verify_onnx.py", "--model", CKPT, "--onnx", f"{OUT}/model.onnx",
    "--dataset", "cifar10-upscaled", "--input-size", "224", "--images", 1000)
## 4 · Summary and download bundle

b, f, t = r["baseline"], r["stages"][-1], r["totals"]
print(f"parameters: {b['parameters']:,} -> {f['parameters']:,}")
print(f"accuracy  : {b['accuracy']*100:.2f}% -> {f['accuracy']*100:.2f}%   (drop {t['accuracy_drop_pp']:.2f} pp, on {TEST_IMAGES} test images)")
print(f"size      : {b['size_mb']:.1f} MB -> {f['size_mb']:.1f} MB   ({t['size_reduction']:.1f}x smaller)")
print(f"precision : {f['precision']}")
print("NOTE: latency in this run is Kaggle-CPU latency, not your device. Measure on the target: compresskit bench model.onnx --input-shape 1 3 224 224")

import zipfile
with zipfile.ZipFile(f"{OUT}/vgg16_cifar10_compressed.zip", "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    for name in ("model.onnx", "report.html", "results.json"):
        z.write(f"{OUT}/{name}", name)
print("bundle:", f"{OUT}/vgg16_cifar10_compressed.zip", f"({os.path.getsize(f'{OUT}/vgg16_cifar10_compressed.zip')/1e6:.1f} MB)")

## 5 · On your Mac (real speed check, once)

```bash
unzip vgg16_cifar10_compressed.zip
compresskit bench model.onnx --input-shape 1 3 224 224
```

notebooks.title: VGG-16-BN on ImageNet
notebooks.blurb: Compress pretrained VGG-16-BN using ImageNet data. Requires the dataset described in the notebook; no result for this recipe is claimed here.

cells.source:
# Compress VGG-16-BN (ImageNet, 528 MB) — Kaggle notebook

`torchvision VGG-16-BN (pretrained)  →  gradual prune + fine-tune  →  INT8 quantize  →  ONNX  →  verify against the original`

The step up from the CIFAR notebooks: **138 M parameters, 528 MB, 224×224 inputs**. The same pipeline, no model-specific code.

**Before Run All** (right panel): *Accelerator → GPU T4*, *Internet → On* (downloads the pretrained weights),
and *Add Input* an ImageNet dataset laid out as `train/<class>/*` and `val/<class>/*` with **all 1000 class folders**
(the cell below searches `/kaggle/input` and stops with a clear message if it finds none).

Accuracy is measured on a fixed 2000-image slice of the validation set (the full 50,000 on CPU would take hours at every stage),
so differences under about 1 pp are noise.

Everything lands in `/kaggle/working/` — download `vgg16_compressed.zip` from the *Output* tab.

# ======================= CONFIG =======================
ARCH        = "tv:vgg16_bn"   # any torchvision ImageNet model: tv:resnet152, tv:vgg19_bn, ...
PRUNE_RATIO = 0.5    # fraction of channels removed (0.5 -> ~75% fewer parameters)
STEPS       = 3      # gradual pruning steps
FT_EPOCHS   = 1      # fine-tune epochs after every step (each epoch is a pass over the train split)
LOSS        = "dkd"  # "kd" | "dkd"
BATCH       = 32
CALIB       = 256    # calibration images for INT8 (train split)
TEST_IMAGES = 2000   # validation images used to score every stage
# ======================================================

import os, subprocess, sys, json, shutil, pathlib
REPO = "https://github.com/Bhagyesh0603/Model-Compression-ToolKit..git"
if not os.path.exists("/kaggle/working/ck"):
    subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", REPO, "/kaggle/working/ck"], check=True)
os.chdir("/kaggle/working/ck")
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "-e", "."], check=True)

import torch
print("GPU:", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else "NONE -> fine-tuning will run on CPU and take very long; enable a GPU, then Restart & Run All")

def find_imagenet_root(base="/kaggle/input"):
    """First directory that has train/ and val/ with 1000 class folders each."""
    for dirpath, dirnames, _ in os.walk(base):
        if {"train", "val"} <= set(dirnames):
            counts = [sum(os.path.isdir(os.path.join(dirpath, s, d)) for d in os.listdir(os.path.join(dirpath, s)))
                      for s in ("train", "val")]
            if counts == [1000, 1000]:
                return dirpath
        if dirpath.count(os.sep) - base.count(os.sep) >= 4:
            dirnames[:] = []
    return None

DATA_ROOT = find_imagenet_root()
assert DATA_ROOT, ("No ImageNet-layout dataset under /kaggle/input. Add one with train/<class>/ and val/<class>/ "
                   "(all 1000 classes) via Add Input, then re-run.")
print("ImageNet root:", DATA_ROOT)

def run(*args):
    args = [str(a) for a in args]
    print("$", " ".join(args), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(args).returncode
## 1 · Save the pretrained original (the reference to verify against)

from compresskit.zoo.torchvision_models import build_torchvision
from compresskit.zoo.train import save_model
original = build_torchvision(ARCH)
os.makedirs("checkpoints", exist_ok=True)
CKPT = "checkpoints/vgg16_bn_imagenet.pt"
save_model(original, CKPT, {"arch": ARCH, "dataset": "imagenet", "input_shape": [1, 3, 224, 224]})
print(f"{sum(p.numel() for p in original.parameters()):,} parameters -> {CKPT}")
## 2 · Compress: gradual prune + fine-tune → INT8 → evaluate the .onnx

OUT = "/kaggle/working"
code_ = run(sys.executable, "-m", "compresskit.cli", "pipeline",
            "--model", CKPT, "--dataset", "imagenet", "--data-root", DATA_ROOT,
            "--test-samples", TEST_IMAGES, "--calib", CALIB, "--batch-size", BATCH,
            "--prune", PRUNE_RATIO, "--steps", STEPS, "--fine-tune-epochs", FT_EPOCHS, "--loss", LOSS,
            "--precision", "int8", "--allow-slow-int8",
            "--workdir", f"{OUT}/work", "--report", f"{OUT}/report.html", "--json", f"{OUT}/results.json")
assert code_ == 0, "pipeline failed - read the log above"
## 3 · Does the compressed model actually work? (original vs ONNX on real validation images)

r = json.load(open(f"{OUT}/results.json"))
shutil.copy(r["stages"][-1]["artifact"], f"{OUT}/model.onnx")
run(sys.executable, "experiments/verify_onnx.py", "--model", CKPT, "--onnx", f"{OUT}/model.onnx",
    "--dataset", "imagenet", "--data-root", DATA_ROOT, "--images", 1000)
## 4 · Summary and download bundle

b, f, t = r["baseline"], r["stages"][-1], r["totals"]
print(f"parameters: {b['parameters']:,} -> {f['parameters']:,}")
print(f"accuracy  : {b['accuracy']*100:.2f}% -> {f['accuracy']*100:.2f}%   (drop {t['accuracy_drop_pp']:.2f} pp, on {TEST_IMAGES} val images)")
print(f"size      : {b['size_mb']:.1f} MB -> {f['size_mb']:.1f} MB   ({t['size_reduction']:.1f}x smaller)")
print(f"precision : {f['precision']}")
print("NOTE: latency in this run is Kaggle-CPU latency, not your device. Measure on the target: compresskit bench model.onnx --input-shape 1 3 224 224")

import zipfile
with zipfile.ZipFile(f"{OUT}/vgg16_compressed.zip", "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    for name in ("model.onnx", "report.html", "results.json"):
        z.write(f"{OUT}/{name}", name)
print("bundle:", f"{OUT}/vgg16_compressed.zip", f"({os.path.getsize(f'{OUT}/vgg16_compressed.zip')/1e6:.1f} MB)")

## 5 · On your Mac (real speed check, once)

```bash
unzip vgg16_compressed.zip
compresskit bench model.onnx --input-shape 1 3 224 224
```

notebooks.title: GPU validation
notebooks.blurb: Check CUDA support and exercise a short compression workflow. This is a validation recipe, not a full accuracy benchmark.

cells.source:
# compresskit — GPU validation notebook (Kaggle or Colab)

Checks that the large-model changes really work on a **CUDA GPU**, then runs a short end-to-end compression with timings.
Those code paths (fp16 AMP, auto batch-size probe, Taylor pruning on GPU, per-step checkpoints) can only be tested on a GPU.

| # | Check | What it proves |
|---|-------|----------------|
| 1 | unit tests | the test-suite passes on this machine |
| 2 | AMP speed | fp16 autocast runs and is faster than fp32 (`img/s` for both) |
| 3 | batch probe | `fit_batch_size` finds a batch that fits, and leaves BatchNorm statistics untouched |
| 4 | data path | 32→224 GPU upscaling feeds the model (`img/s`) |
| 5 | Taylor pruning | importance backward pass runs on the GPU without OOM |
| 6 | end to end | short head fine-tune → gradual prune + fine-tune → INT8 → ONNX, a checkpoint saved per step |

**Kaggle:** *Accelerator → GPU T4*, *Internet → On*, optionally *Add Input → CIFAR-10* (python-pickle, has `cifar-10-batches-py`).
**Colab:** *Runtime → Change runtime type → T4 GPU*. CIFAR-10 downloads (170 MB).

This is a **mechanics test, not a benchmark**: the end-to-end part trains the new head for only a few hundred batches
and fine-tunes for a few batches per step, so its accuracy numbers show the pipeline works, not the final quality.
Change `ARCH` to test another model (`tv:resnet152`, `tv:densenet121`, `tv:convnext_tiny`, `tv:vgg16_bn`).

# ======================= CONFIG =======================
ARCH           = "tv:resnet50"   # try: tv:resnet152, tv:densenet121, tv:convnext_tiny, tv:vgg16_bn
REQUIRE_GPU    = True            # stop at once if no CUDA GPU is attached
PRUNE_RATIO    = 0.5
STEPS          = 2               # gradual pruning steps
HEAD_BATCHES   = 150             # batches used to train the new 10-class head
FT_BATCHES     = 40              # training batches per fine-tune epoch after each prune step
REQUESTED_BATCH = 64             # effective training batch; the probe may split it into micro-batches
TEST_IMAGES    = 500             # test images used to score every stage
CALIB          = 128             # calibration images (BN, INT8, Taylor)
# ======================================================

import os, subprocess, sys, json, shutil, time, copy, itertools, pathlib
IN_COLAB = "COLAB_RELEASE_TAG" in os.environ or os.path.exists("/content")
WORK = "/content" if IN_COLAB and not os.path.exists("/kaggle/working") else "/kaggle/working"
print("platform:", "Colab" if WORK == "/content" else "Kaggle", "| working dir:", WORK)
REPO = "https://github.com/Bhagyesh0603/Model-Compression-ToolKit..git"
if not os.path.exists(f"{WORK}/ck"):
    subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", REPO, f"{WORK}/ck"], check=True)
os.chdir(f"{WORK}/ck")
# --no-deps: never let pip swap the GPU build of torch that the platform ships; install only what is missing.
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "--no-deps", "-e", "."], check=True)
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "torch-pruning>=1.5,<2.0", "onnx>=1.16", "onnxruntime>=1.19", "matplotlib"], check=True)

import torch

smi = subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi", "-L"], capture_output=True, text=True) if shutil.which("nvidia-smi") else None
print("nvidia-smi:", smi.stdout.strip() if smi is not None and smi.returncode == 0 else "no NVIDIA GPU visible to this session")
CUDA = torch.cuda.is_available()
print("GPU:", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if CUDA else "NONE")
print("torch", torch.__version__, "| cuda", torch.version.cuda)
if REQUIRE_GPU and not CUDA:
    if smi is not None and smi.returncode == 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"A GPU is attached but this PyTorch build cannot use it (torch {torch.__version__}). Restart the session and Run All again; if it repeats, send me this output.")
    raise SystemExit("No GPU is attached. Kaggle: right panel -> Accelerator -> GPU T4, then Restart & Run All.  Colab: Runtime -> Change runtime type -> T4 GPU.")
assert os.path.exists("compresskit/core/amp.py"), "this clone is missing the large-model changes - push them to GitHub first"
## 1 · Unit tests on this machine

r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "tests", "-q", "-x", "-p", "no:cacheprovider"], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(r.stdout[-600:])
check("1 unit tests", r.returncode == 0, r.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1] if r.stdout.strip() else r.stderr[-200:])
## 2 · fp16 AMP vs fp32 training speed (needs CUDA)
## 3 · Auto batch size probe

model = fresh()
before = {k: v.clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
t = time.perf_counter()
fitted = fit_batch_size(model, bundle.input_shape, start=256, device=DEV, teacher=model)
micro, accum = split_batch(REQUESTED_BATCH, fitted)
model.cpu()
bn_same = all(torch.equal(v, before[k]) for k, v in model.state_dict().items())
print(f"largest batch that fits at 224x224: {fitted}   ({time.perf_counter() - t:.1f}s)")
print(f"requested effective batch {REQUESTED_BATCH} -> micro-batch {micro} x {accum} accumulation steps")
check("3 batch probe", fitted >= 1 and bn_same, f"fits {fitted}; BN stats {'untouched' if bn_same else 'MODIFIED'}")
del model
## 4 · Data path (GPU upscaling)

loader = bundle.train_loader(batch_size=micro)
n_batches = 30
it = iter(loader); next(it)
sync(); t = time.perf_counter(); seen = 0
for _ in range(n_batches):
    x, y = next(it); seen += len(x)
sync()
rate = seen / (time.perf_counter() - t)
print(f"train loader: {rate:.0f} img/s   batch {tuple(x.shape)} on {x.device}")
check("4 data path", x.shape[-1] == 224 and rate > 0, f"{rate:.0f} img/s, batch on {x.device}")
del it, loader
## 5 · Taylor pruning on the GPU

from compresskit.pruning.prune import prune
calib = bundle.calibration_loader(n=CALIB, batch_size=min(micro, 32))
net = fresh().cpu().eval()
reset_peak(); t = time.perf_counter()
try:
    pruned, stats = prune(net, torch.randn(*bundle.input_shape), ratio=PRUNE_RATIO, align=16, steps=1,
                          criterion="taylor", loader=calib, batches=2)
    removed = 1 - sum(p.numel() for p in pruned.parameters()) / sum(p.numel() for p in net.parameters())
    print(f"{stats.summary()}\n{time.perf_counter() - t:.1f}s, peak GPU memory {peak_gb():.2f} GB")
    check("5 Taylor pruning", removed > 0.3, f"{removed * 100:.0f}% params removed, peak {peak_gb():.2f} GB")
except Exception as e:

del net

from compresskit.pipeline import Pipeline
from compresskit.zoo.train import TrainConfig, train

test_loader = bundle.test_loader(batch_size=micro)

train(original, Few(train_loader, HEAD_BATCHES),

print(f"head fine-tune: {time.perf_counter() - t0:.0f}s")

                input_shape=bundle.input_shape, workdir=work, warmup=5, runs=20, device=DEV, accum_steps=accum)

t0 = time.perf_counter()
try:
    result = pipe.run()
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0
    print(); print(result.summary()); print(f"pipeline wall time: {elapsed:.0f}s")
    ckpts = sorted(p.name for p in pathlib.Path(work).glob("prune_step*.pt"))

# Compress ResNet-152 (232 MB, 58 M parameters) on CIFAR-10 — Kaggle or Colab notebook (Member 1)

`ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-152  →  new 10-class head, fine-tuned on CIFAR-10  →  gradual prune + fine-tune  →  INT8  →  ONNX  →  verify`

**Why this model is hard to compress:** the deepest standard residual network: 152 layers, bottleneck blocks, and every residual add forces the pruner to keep whole groups of channels aligned.
**What to watch:** Residual ties: layers joined by a skip connection must be pruned together, so one bad ratio on a stage drags several layers.

CIFAR-10 images are upscaled 32→224 so the network keeps its real size; upscaling adds no detail, it only makes the model big.

**Kaggle — before Run All** (right panel): *Accelerator → GPU T4*, *Internet → On* (downloads the pretrained weights),
and *Add Input → CIFAR-10* in the python-pickle format (it must contain a `cifar-10-batches-py` folder). Without it the notebook
downloads CIFAR-10 itself, which took about 50 minutes on a slow Kaggle link before.

**Colab — before Run All:** *Runtime → Change runtime type → T4 GPU*. There is no "Add Input", so CIFAR-10 always downloads (170 MB).
At the end the zip is offered as a browser download. The notebook detects which platform it is on by itself.

Batch size, mixed precision (fp16) and the GPU placement of every step are automatic; if a GPU run still reports
"out of GPU memory", set `BATCH` to a smaller number. A pruned checkpoint is saved after every step under `work/`.

Time: the 224×224 training passes dominate. Expect hours, not minutes, on a T4; lower `TRAIN_EPOCHS` / `STEPS` to shorten it
(Kaggle sessions stop after 12 h). Accuracy is scored on a fixed 2000-image slice of the test set, so differences under about 1 pp are noise.

Everything lands in `/kaggle/working/` — download `resnet152_cifar10_compressed.zip` from the *Output* tab (Kaggle) or the browser download prompt (Colab).

# ======================= CONFIG =======================
ARCH         = "tv:resnet152"  # any torchvision ImageNet model: tv:resnet152, tv:densenet121, tv:convnext_tiny, tv:efficientnet_b0, ...
TRAIN_EPOCHS = 2      # fine-tune the pretrained model on CIFAR-10 (the "original" we compress)
PRUNE_RATIO  = 0.5    # fraction of channels removed (0.5 -> ~75% fewer parameters)
STEPS        = 3      # gradual pruning steps
FT_EPOCHS    = 1      # fine-tune epochs after every step
LOSS         = "dkd"  # "kd" | "dkd"
BATCH        = "auto"   # "auto" probes the GPU for the largest batch that fits and accumulates up to 64
CRITERION    = "taylor"  # channel importance: "taylor" (loss-aware, GPU) | "magnitude" (fast)
PROTECT      = 2        # prune the 2 most quantization-sensitive layers at half the ratio (0 = off)
CALIB        = 256    # calibration images for INT8 (train split)
TEST_IMAGES  = 2000   # test images used to score every stage
# ======================================================

import os, subprocess, sys, json, shutil, pathlib
IN_COLAB = "COLAB_RELEASE_TAG" in os.environ or os.path.exists("/content")
WORK = "/content" if IN_COLAB and not os.path.exists("/kaggle/working") else "/kaggle/working"
print("platform:", "Colab" if WORK == "/content" else "Kaggle", "| working dir:", WORK)
REPO = "https://github.com/Bhagyesh0603/Model-Compression-ToolKit..git"
if not os.path.exists(f"{WORK}/ck"):
    subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", REPO, f"{WORK}/ck"], check=True)
os.chdir(f"{WORK}/ck")
# --no-deps: never let pip swap the GPU build of torch that the platform ships; install only what is missing.
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "--no-deps", "-e", "."], check=True)
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "torch-pruning>=1.5,<2.0", "onnx>=1.16", "onnxruntime>=1.19", "matplotlib"], check=True)

import torch

smi = subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi", "-L"], capture_output=True, text=True) if shutil.which("nvidia-smi") else None
print("nvidia-smi:", smi.stdout.strip() if smi is not None and smi.returncode == 0 else "no NVIDIA GPU visible to this session")
print("GPU:", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else "NONE -> training would take days on CPU; enable a GPU (Kaggle: right panel; Colab: Runtime > Change runtime type), then Restart & Run All")
from compresskit.zoo.data import resolve_root
print("CIFAR-10 location:", resolve_root(), "(attached dataset if under /kaggle/input, else it will download)")

def run(*args):
    args = [str(a) for a in args]
    print("$", " ".join(args), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(args).returncode

DATA = ["--dataset", "cifar10-upscaled", "--input-size", "224", "--test-samples", str(TEST_IMAGES)]
## 1 · The original: pretrained ResNet-152 with a CIFAR-10 head, fine-tuned

CKPT = "checkpoints/resnet152_cifar10.pt"
assert run(sys.executable, "-m", "compresskit.cli", "train", "--arch", ARCH, *DATA,
           "--epochs", TRAIN_EPOCHS, "--lr", "0.01", "--batch-size", BATCH, "--out", CKPT) == 0, "training failed - read the log above"
## 2 · Compress: gradual prune + fine-tune → INT8 → evaluate the .onnx

OUT = WORK
code_ = run(sys.executable, "-m", "compresskit.cli", "pipeline", "--model", CKPT, *DATA,
            "--calib", CALIB, "--batch-size", BATCH,
            "--criterion", CRITERION, "--protect-sensitive", PROTECT,
            "--prune", PRUNE_RATIO, "--steps", STEPS, "--fine-tune-epochs", FT_EPOCHS, "--loss", LOSS,
            "--precision", "int8", "--allow-slow-int8",
            "--workdir", f"{OUT}/work", "--report", f"{OUT}/report.html", "--json", f"{OUT}/results.json")
assert code_ == 0, "pipeline failed - read the log above"
## 3 · Does the compressed model actually work? (original vs ONNX on real test images)

r = json.load(open(f"{OUT}/results.json"))
shutil.copy(r["stages"][-1]["artifact"], f"{OUT}/model.onnx")
run(sys.executable, "experiments/verify_onnx.py", "--model", CKPT, "--onnx", f"{OUT}/model.onnx",
    "--dataset", "cifar10-upscaled", "--input-size", "224", "--images", 1000)
## 4 · Summary and download bundle

b, f, t = r["baseline"], r["stages"][-1], r["totals"]
print(f"parameters: {b['parameters']:,} -> {f['parameters']:,}")
print(f"accuracy  : {b['accuracy']*100:.2f}% -> {f['accuracy']*100:.2f}%   (drop {t['accuracy_drop_pp']:.2f} pp, on {TEST_IMAGES} test images)")
print(f"size      : {b['size_mb']:.1f} MB -> {f['size_mb']:.1f} MB   ({t['size_reduction']:.1f}x smaller)")
print(f"precision : {f['precision']}")
print("NOTE: latency in this run is Kaggle-CPU latency, not your device. Measure on the target: compresskit bench model.onnx --input-shape 1 3 224 224")

import zipfile
with zipfile.ZipFile(f"{OUT}/resnet152_cifar10_compressed.zip", "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    for name in ("model.onnx", "report.html", "results.json"):
        z.write(f"{OUT}/{name}", name)
print("bundle:", f"{OUT}/resnet152_cifar10_compressed.zip", f"({os.path.getsize(f'{OUT}/resnet152_cifar10_compressed.zip')/1e6:.1f} MB)")

if WORK == "/content":
    from google.colab import files
    files.download(f"{OUT}/resnet152_cifar10_compressed.zip")

## 5 · On your Mac (real speed check, once)

```bash
unzip resnet152_cifar10_compressed.zip
compresskit bench model.onnx --input-shape 1 3 224 224
```

# Compress ConvNeXt-Tiny (109 MB, 28 M parameters) on CIFAR-10 — Kaggle or Colab notebook (Member 3)

`ImageNet-pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny  →  new 10-class head, fine-tuned on CIFAR-10  →  gradual prune + fine-tune  →  INT8  →  ONNX  →  verify`

**Why this model is hard to compress:** a modern CNN: 7x7 depthwise convolutions, LayerNorm and GELU instead of BatchNorm and ReLU. Both pruning and INT8 are less forgiving here than on classic ResNets.
**What to watch:** No BatchNorm, depthwise convs and LayerNorm: INT8 quantization of ConvNeXt is known to lose more accuracy than ResNet-style nets.

CIFAR-10 images are upscaled 32→224 so the network keeps its real size; upscaling adds no detail, it only makes the model big.

**Kaggle — before Run All** (right panel): *Accelerator → GPU T4*, *Internet → On* (downloads the pretrained weights),
and *Add Input → CIFAR-10* in the python-pickle format (it must contain a `cifar-10-batches-py` folder). Without it the notebook
downloads CIFAR-10 itself, which took about 50 minutes on a slow Kaggle link before.

**Colab — before Run All:** *Runtime → Change runtime type → T4 GPU*. There is no "Add Input", so CIFAR-10 always downloads (170 MB).
At the end the zip is offered as a browser download. The notebook detects which platform it is on by itself.

Batch size, mixed precision (fp16) and the GPU placement of every step are automatic; if a GPU run still reports
"out of GPU memory", set `BATCH` to a smaller number. A pruned checkpoint is saved after every step under `work/`.

Time: the 224×224 training passes dominate. Expect hours, not minutes, on a T4; lower `TRAIN_EPOCHS` / `STEPS` to shorten it
(Kaggle sessions stop after 12 h). Accuracy is scored on a fixed 2000-image slice of the test set, so differences under about 1 pp are noise.

Everything lands in `/kaggle/working/` — download `convnext_tiny_cifar10_compressed.zip` from the *Output* tab (Kaggle) or the browser download prompt (Colab).

# ======================= CONFIG =======================
ARCH         = "tv:convnext_tiny"  # any torchvision ImageNet model: tv:resnet152, tv:densenet121, tv:convnext_tiny, tv:efficientnet_b0, ...
TRAIN_EPOCHS = 2      # fine-tune the pretrained model on CIFAR-10 (the "original" we compress)
PRUNE_RATIO  = 0.5    # fraction of channels removed (0.5 -> ~75% fewer parameters)
STEPS        = 3      # gradual pruning steps
FT_EPOCHS    = 1      # fine-tune epochs after every step
LOSS         = "dkd"  # "kd" | "dkd"
BATCH        = "auto"   # "auto" probes the GPU for the largest batch that fits and accumulates up to 64
CRITERION    = "taylor"  # channel importance: "taylor" (loss-aware, GPU) | "magnitude" (fast)
PROTECT      = 2        # prune the 2 most quantization-sensitive layers at half the ratio (0 = off)
CALIB        = 256    # calibration images for INT8 (train split)
TEST_IMAGES  = 2000   # test images used to score every stage
# ======================================================

import os, subprocess, sys, json, shutil, pathlib
IN_COLAB = "COLAB_RELEASE_TAG" in os.environ or os.path.exists("/content")
WORK = "/content" if IN_COLAB and not os.path.exists("/kaggle/working") else "/kaggle/working"
print("platform:", "Colab" if WORK == "/content" else "Kaggle", "| working dir:", WORK)
REPO = "https://github.com/Bhagyesh0603/Model-Compression-ToolKit..git"
if not os.path.exists(f"{WORK}/ck"):
    subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", REPO, f"{WORK}/ck"], check=True)
os.chdir(f"{WORK}/ck")
# --no-deps: never let pip swap the GPU build of torch that the platform ships; install only what is missing.
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "--no-deps", "-e", "."], check=True)
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "torch-pruning>=1.5,<2.0", "onnx>=1.16", "onnxruntime>=1.19", "matplotlib"], check=True)

import torch

smi = subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi", "-L"], capture_output=True, text=True) if shutil.which("nvidia-smi") else None
print("nvidia-smi:", smi.stdout.strip() if smi is not None and smi.returncode == 0 else "no NVIDIA GPU visible to this session")
print("GPU:", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else "NONE -> training would take days on CPU; enable a GPU (Kaggle: right panel; Colab: Runtime > Change runtime type), then Restart & Run All")
from compresskit.zoo.data import resolve_root
print("CIFAR-10 location:", resolve_root(), "(attached dataset if under /kaggle/input, else it will download)")

def run(*args):
    args = [str(a) for a in args]
    print("$", " ".join(args), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(args).returncode

DATA = ["--dataset", "cifar10-upscaled", "--input-size", "224", "--test-samples", str(TEST_IMAGES)]
## 1 · The original: pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny with a CIFAR-10 head, fine-tuned

CKPT = "checkpoints/convnext_tiny_cifar10.pt"
assert run(sys.executable, "-m", "compresskit.cli", "train", "--arch", ARCH, *DATA,
           "--epochs", TRAIN_EPOCHS, "--lr", "0.003", "--batch-size", BATCH, "--out", CKPT) == 0, "training failed - read the log above"
## 2 · Compress: gradual prune + fine-tune → INT8 → evaluate the .onnx

OUT = WORK
code_ = run(sys.executable, "-m", "compresskit.cli", "pipeline", "--model", CKPT, *DATA,
            "--calib", CALIB, "--batch-size", BATCH,
            "--criterion", CRITERION, "--protect-sensitive", PROTECT,
            "--prune", PRUNE_RATIO, "--steps", STEPS, "--fine-tune-epochs", FT_EPOCHS, "--loss", LOSS,
            "--precision", "int8", "--allow-slow-int8",
            "--workdir", f"{OUT}/work", "--report", f"{OUT}/report.html", "--json", f"{OUT}/results.json")
assert code_ == 0, "pipeline failed - read the log above"
## 3 · Does the compressed model actually work? (original vs ONNX on real test images)

r = json.load(open(f"{OUT}/results.json"))
shutil.copy(r["stages"][-1]["artifact"], f"{OUT}/model.onnx")
run(sys.executable, "experiments/verify_onnx.py", "--model", CKPT, "--onnx", f"{OUT}/model.onnx",
    "--dataset", "cifar10-upscaled", "--input-size", "224", "--images", 1000)
## 4 · Summary and download bundle

b, f, t = r["baseline"], r["stages"][-1], r["totals"]
print(f"parameters: {b['parameters']:,} -> {f['parameters']:,}")
print(f"accuracy  : {b['accuracy']*100:.2f}% -> {f['accuracy']*100:.2f}%   (drop {t['accuracy_drop_pp']:.2f} pp, on {TEST_IMAGES} test images)")
print(f"size      : {b['size_mb']:.1f} MB -> {f['size_mb']:.1f} MB   ({t['size_reduction']:.1f}x smaller)")
print(f"precision : {f['precision']}")
print("NOTE: latency in this run is Kaggle-CPU latency, not your device. Measure on the target: compresskit bench model.onnx --input-shape 1 3 224 224")

import zipfile
with zipfile.ZipFile(f"{OUT}/convnext_tiny_cifar10_compressed.zip", "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    for name in ("model.onnx", "report.html", "results.json"):
        z.write(f"{OUT}/{name}", name)
print("bundle:", f"{OUT}/convnext_tiny_cifar10_compressed.zip", f"({os.path.getsize(f'{OUT}/convnext_tiny_cifar10_compressed.zip')/1e6:.1f} MB)")

if WORK == "/content":
    from google.colab import files
    files.download(f"{OUT}/convnext_tiny_cifar10_compressed.zip")

## 5 · On your Mac (real speed check, once)

```bash
unzip convnext_tiny_cifar10_compressed.zip
compresskit bench model.onnx --input-shape 1 3 224 224
```
